title_he: לֹא מֵחֹשֶׁךְ אֲנַחְנוּ וְלֹא מִלֵּיל אָפֵל

lines: לֹא מֵחֹשֶׁךְ אֲנַחְנוּ וְלֹא מִלֵּיל אָפֵל

review: The hymn is 1 John 2:15–17 in the wilderness: 1:1–4 is 1 Thess 5:4–5 (לֹא בַחֹשֶׁךְ … בְּנֵי אוֹר) with 1 John 2:17, 3:1–3 Exod 13:21 (בְּעַמּוּד אֵשׁ … בֶּעָנָן), 4:1–3 Exod 16:4,15 with Ps 78:15–16, 5:1–3 Eph 6:10–13, and 6:1–3 1 Cor 15:52 with 1 John 3:2.

The refrain הָעוֹלָם עֹבֵר וְתַאֲוָתוֹ is 1 John 2:17 almost word for word (וְהָעוֹלָם עֹבֵר וְתַאֲוָתוֹ), and is repeated in all six stanzas because the Arabic repeats الْعَالَمُ يَمْضِي وَشَهْوَتُهُ. The Hebrew keeps the singular 'its lust' rather than a plural, since the verse's point is the one desire that passes.

1:1 לֹא מֵחֹשֶׁךְ … מִלֵּיל אָפֵל — the Arabic لَسْنَا مِنْ ظَلامٍ أَوْ لَيْلٍ دَيْجُور has two nouns; אָפֵל is the biblical adjective for thick darkness (Joel 2:2, יוֹם חֹשֶׁךְ וַאֲפֵלָה), so the line keeps both and does not collapse them into one.

3:3 נוֹסְעִים בַּמִּדְבָּר וּבִשְׁמָמָה — the Arabic سَائِحُونَ فِي الْبَرَارِي وَالْقِفَار is 'journeying in the wastes and desolations'; נָסַע is the wilderness verb of the camp's moving (Num 10:12), and שְׁמָמָה is the prophetic word for the desolate land, so the stanza is Israel's march and not a general pilgrimage.

5:3 בִּכְלֵי אֱלֹהִים — the Arabic بِسِلَاحِ اللهِ is 'with God's weapon'; the Hebrew uses the plural כְּלֵי, the word of the whole armour of Eph 6:11 (כְּלֵי נֶשֶׁק), so the line covers the panoply and not a single sword.
